441	// decodedArchiveFrame is one archive parsed up to, but not including, the
442	// content checks: the reconstructed records and the informational
443	// checkpoint embedded in the header. Nothing at this stage has been
444	// validated against the caller's organization or retained checkpoint.
445	type decodedArchiveFrame struct {
446		records     []AuditRecord
447		org         string
448		endSeq      int
449		fingerprint string
450	}
451	
452	// decodeAuditArchiveFrame parses one frame's framing, checksum and payload.
453	// It performs no content validation: the embedded organization and
454	// checkpoint are returned for the caller to compare, and the records are
455	// not chain-checked until a content-validating entry point runs the single
456	// VerifyAudit pass.
457	func decodeAuditArchiveFrame(archive []byte) (decodedArchiveFrame, error) {
458		magicLen := len(archiveMagic)
459		if len(archive) < magicLen+4+sha256.Size || string(archive[:magicLen]) != archiveMagic {
460			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: unrecognized audit archive", ErrInvalidArchive)
461		}
462		pos := magicLen
463		payloadLen := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(archive[pos : pos+4]))
464		pos += 4
465		checksumEnd := pos + payloadLen
466		if payloadLen < 0 || checksumEnd+sha256.Size != len(archive) {
467			// A short frame is truncation; bytes beyond the one frame (a
468			// concatenated second archive, junk appended to a good file) are a
469			// framing failure too.
470			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: truncated or trailing audit archive bytes", ErrInvalidArchive)
471		}
472		payload := archive[pos:checksumEnd]
473		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
474		if !bytes.Equal(sum[:], archive[checksumEnd:checksumEnd+sha256.Size]) {
475			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: checksum mismatch", ErrInvalidArchive)
476		}
477	
478		r := &archiveReader{data: payload}
479		embeddedOrg := r.stringField()
480		embeddedEndSeq := r.u32()
481		embeddedFingerprint := r.stringField()
482		// Every record writes two payload markers, a sequence word, two
483		// fingerprint length words and org/kind length words: 22 bytes even
484		// when every string is empty.
485		n := r.boundedCount(22)
486		if r.err != nil {
487			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, r.err
488		}
489		records := make([]AuditRecord, 0, n)
490		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
491			// Read the outer fields in the single record field table's (write
492			// and fingerprint) order, so a field can never be restored into the
493			// wrong member or skipped.
494			var rec AuditRecord
495			for j := range recordFields {
496				f := &recordFields[j]
497				switch f.kind {
498				case recordFieldString:
499					f.setString(&rec, r.stringField())
500				case recordFieldInt:
501					f.setInt(&rec, r.u32())
502				case recordFieldChange:
503					f.setChange(&rec, r.change())
504				case recordFieldDecision:
505					f.setDecision(&rec, r.decisionRecord())
506				}
507			}
508			records = append(records, rec)
509		}
510		if r.err != nil {
511			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, r.err
512		}
513		if r.pos != len(payload) {
514			return decodedArchiveFrame{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d unconsumed archive bytes", ErrInvalidArchive, len(payload)-r.pos)
515		}
516		return decodedArchiveFrame{
517			records:     records,
518			org:         embeddedOrg,
519			endSeq:      embeddedEndSeq,
520			fingerprint: embeddedFingerprint,
521		}, nil
522	}

524	// validateDecodedFrame applies the content checks to a parsed frame and
525	// returns the material as VerifiedAuditMaterial after the single complete
526	// VerifyAudit chain pass. The embedded checkpoint is informational; still,
527	// contradicting the retained checkpoint means the payload was altered, and
528	// the authoritative check always uses the caller's independently retained
529	// checkpoint.
530	func validateDecodedFrame(frame decodedArchiveFrame, org string, cp Checkpoint) (VerifiedAuditMaterial, error) {
531		// Content checks reuse the exact audit-range validation the live export
532		// and offline review paths use, so an archive can never smuggle in a
533		// shape those entry points would reject.
534		if frame.org != org {
535			return VerifiedAuditMaterial{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: archive organization %q does not match %q", ErrInvalidRange, frame.org, org)
536		}
537		if frame.endSeq != cp.EndSeq || frame.fingerprint != cp.Fingerprint {
538			return VerifiedAuditMaterial{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: embedded checkpoint does not match the retained checkpoint", ErrInvalidRange)
539		}
540		return verifyAuditMaterial(org, frame.records, cp)
541	}

543	// DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive reads one archive produced by
544	// EncodeAuditArchive, validates it once, and returns the material ready
545	// for RecheckVerifiedDecisionOffline. It is the single-validation half of
546	// the offline review flow: the returned VerifiedAuditMaterial carries the
547	// already-checked chain, so the following review performs no second chain
548	// pass. org is the organization the caller expects, and cp is the
549	// checkpoint the caller independently retained; the checkpoint embedded in
550	// the file is never treated as evidence, so even an archive carrying a
551	// plausible checkpoint only validates against the one supplied here.
552	//
553	// A missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization. Unrecognized framing,
554	// truncation, a trailing second archive or any other extra byte, a bad
555	// checksum, and undecodable content are ErrInvalidArchive. Records that
556	// decode but are missing, out of order, foreign to the organization,
557	// modified (including a record after the one the caller intends to review)
558	// or mismatched with the supplied checkpoint fail the whole read with
559	// ErrInvalidRange. Failure returns no material. A successful read only
560	// proves the material matches the checkpoint: an original decision that
561	// disagrees with a recomputed one is reported later by offline review, not
562	// treated as archive damage. The material is detached from archive
563	// (mutating one never reaches the other), and the call is read-only.
564	func DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive(archive []byte, org string, cp Checkpoint) (VerifiedAuditMaterial, error) {
565		if org == "" {
566			return VerifiedAuditMaterial{}, ErrMissingOrganization
567		}
568		frame, err := decodeAuditArchiveFrame(archive)
569		if err != nil {
570			return VerifiedAuditMaterial{}, err
571		}
572		return validateDecodedFrame(frame, org, cp)

577	// org is the organization the caller expects, and cp is the checkpoint the

580	// checkpoint only validates against the one supplied here.

583	// chain validation itself and never assumes another entry point ran first.
584	// (The `darksafe review` command instead uses DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive
585	// followed by RecheckVerifiedDecisionOffline, so one invocation validates
586	// the chain exactly once rather than once here and again in the review.)
587	//
588	// A missing organization is ErrMissingOrganization. Unrecognized framing,
589	// truncation, a trailing second archive or any other extra byte, a bad
590	// checksum, and undecodable content are ErrInvalidArchive. Records that
591	// decode but are missing, out of order, foreign to the organization,
592	// modified (including a record after the one the caller intends to review)
593	// or mismatched with the supplied checkpoint fail the whole read with
594	// ErrInvalidRange. Failure returns no records. A successful read only
595	// proves the material matches the checkpoint: an original decision that
596	// disagrees with a recomputed one is reported later by offline review, not
597	// treated as archive damage. The result is detached from archive (mutating
598	// one never reaches the other), and the call is read-only.
599	func DecodeAuditArchive(archive []byte, org string, cp Checkpoint) ([]AuditRecord, error) {
600		m, err := DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive(archive, org, cp)
601		if err != nil {
602			return nil, err
603		}
604		return m.records, nil
605	}

11	// export; later publishes or rollbacks, and a wider later export, cannot
12	// change the recomputed result.
13	//
14	// A review that already holds the material as decoded records
15	// (RecheckDecisionOffline) and one that starts from an archive file
16	// (DecodeAuditArchive followed by a review) historically each ran the full
17	// VerifyAudit chain check on their own, so `darksafe review` validated the
18	// same material twice per invocation. The two stages now share one pass:
19	// VerifyAudit runs exactly once per review, its result is carried in an
20	// unexported VerifiedAuditMaterial, and the review replays the target from
21	// that already-verified material without re-checking the chain. The
22	// standalone entry points keep validating their own inputs, so neither
23	// requires the caller to have run another entry point first.
24	package darksafe
25	
26	import "fmt"
27	
28	// OfflineDecisionReview compares the decision stored in an audited record
29	// with a decision recomputed purely from the exported material.
30	type OfflineDecisionReview struct {
31		// Seq is the reviewed decision record's sequence.
32		Seq int
33		// Original is the decision preserved in the audited record.
34		Original Decision
35		// Recomputed is the decision evaluated again offline from the saved
36		// request and the policy version it originally used.
37		Recomputed Decision
38		// Consistent reports whether both decisions agree on every field
39		// (allowance, reason, matched policies and version), treating a nil
40		// matched list and an empty matched list as the same.
41		Consistent bool
42	}
43	
44	// VerifiedAuditMaterial is an export that has passed the complete
45	// VerifyAudit chain check against the checkpoint it carries. It is the
46	// boundary between one validation and the review: an entry point that has
47	// just validated the material hands it to RecheckVerifiedDecisionOffline,
48	// and the review replays the target without validating the chain a second
49	// time.
50	//
51	// It is intentionally unexported: it can only be produced by this package's
52	// own validating entry points (verifyAuditMaterial, reached from
53	// RecheckDecisionOffline, DecodeAuditArchive and DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive),
54	// never from a caller's assertion. It carries no memo that survives the
55	// call that produced it, so modified material or a different checkpoint
56	// always forces a fresh validation; the embedded records are the caller's
57	// and stay owned by the caller.
58	type VerifiedAuditMaterial struct {
59		org     string
60		records []AuditRecord
61		cp      Checkpoint
62	}
63	
64	// verifyAuditMaterial validates the whole export exactly as VerifyAudit
65	// does and, on success, returns it as VerifiedAuditMaterial. It is the
66	// single place the chain check is performed on the offline review path; a
67	// failure returns no material, so a later stage can never review records
68	// that did not validate.
69	func verifyAuditMaterial(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) (VerifiedAuditMaterial, error) {
70		if verifyAuditObserver != nil {
71			verifyAuditObserver()
72		}
73		if err := VerifyAudit(org, records, cp); err != nil {
74			return VerifiedAuditMaterial{}, err
75		}
76		return VerifiedAuditMaterial{org: org, records: records, cp: cp}, nil
77	}
78	
79	// RecheckVerifiedDecisionOffline re-evaluates one decision record from
80	// material a preceding stage has already chain-validated as one unit
81	// (verifyAuditMaterial or DecodeVerifiedAuditArchive). It does not run the
82	// chain check again: one review performs one complete chain validation, and
83	// tampering anywhere is rejected before this stage is reached. All target
84	// and replay guarantees are otherwise identical to
85	// RecheckDecisionOffline's: ErrAuditNotFound for a non-positive or absent
86	// target sequence, ErrAuditNotADecision when the target is a policy change
87	// record, and ErrVersionNotFound when the version the decision names has no
88	// change record before the target (including content that appears only
89	// after it); a newer version is never substituted. The call is read-only
90	// and the returned decisions are detached from the material's slices.
91	func RecheckVerifiedDecisionOffline(m VerifiedAuditMaterial, seq int) (OfflineDecisionReview, error) {
92		return recheckVerifiedOffline(m, seq)
93	}
94	
95	// recheckVerifiedOffline is the shared review body. It takes an unexported
96	// verified-material value so only this package's validating stages can
97	// reach the already-validated path; standalone RecheckDecisionOffline
98	// validates first and then calls it just as the combined archive flow does.
99	func recheckVerifiedOffline(m VerifiedAuditMaterial, seq int) (OfflineDecisionReview, error) {
100		org, records := m.org, m.records
101		if seq < 1 {
102			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, seq)
103		}
104		if seq > len(records) {
105			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: export ends at %d, no sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, len(records), seq)
106		}
107		rec := &records[seq-1]
108		if rec.Kind != AuditDecision || rec.Decision == nil {
109			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d is %s", ErrAuditNotADecision, seq, rec.Kind)
110		}
111	
112		original := cloneDecisionValue(rec.Decision.Decision)
113		req := rec.Decision.Request
114		// Detach the request list by non-nil rather than by length: a non-nil
115		// empty role list with spare capacity must not be shared back with the
116		// caller's material, even though evaluation never reads any element.
117		req.Subject.Roles = cloneStrings(req.Subject.Roles)
118		version := original.Version
119	
120		// The version's full content must travel in a same-organization policy
121		// change record positioned before the decision. The replay core resolves
122		// the version before replaying any request rule, so a request the
123		// envelope rejects cannot mask a missing or later-only version.
124		resolve := func(want int) versionPolicies {
125			if policies, found := policiesBefore(records, seq-1, want); found {
126				return versionPolicies{policies: policies}
127			}
128			if _, later := policiesBefore(records, len(records), want); later {
129				return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAfterTarget}
130			}
131			return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAbsent}
132		}
133		recomputed, status := replayRecordedDecision(org, req, version, resolve)
134		switch status {
135		case replayVersionAfterTarget:
136			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf(
137				"%w: decision at sequence %d used version %d, whose change record appears only after it",
138				ErrVersionNotFound, seq, version)
139		case replayVersionAbsent:
140			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, fmt.Errorf(
141				"%w: decision at sequence %d used version %d, which has no policy change record in the export",
142				ErrVersionNotFound, seq, version)
143		}
144	
145		return OfflineDecisionReview{
146			Seq:        seq,
147			Original:   original,
148			Recomputed: recomputed,
149			Consistent: decisionsEqual(original, recomputed),
150		}, nil
151	}
152	
153	// RecheckDecisionOffline re-evaluates one decision record offline. org is
154	// the organization name, records is its complete export starting at
155	// sequence 1 (a valid prefix is sufficient when paired with its own
156	// checkpoint), cp is the separately saved checkpoint, and seq identifies
157	// the decision record to review. The call is read-only: it neither mutates
158	// the supplied material nor appends audit records, and the returned
159	// decisions are detached from the input slices.
160	//
161	// The entire export is chain-validated in this call before any result is
162	// produced; tampering anywhere, including in records after the target,
163	// fails the review. The caller does not need to have validated the
164	// material through another entry point first: standalone callers receive
165	// the exact same guarantees DecodeAuditArchive gives, and validation is
166	// always based on this call's material, organization and checkpoint — a
167	// previous validation is never reused after the material changes or the
168	// checkpoint changes. Distinguishable errors follow the other audit entry
169	// points: ErrMissingOrganization for an empty organization, ErrAuditNotFound
170	// for a non-positive or absent target sequence, and ErrAuditNotADecision
171	// when the target is a policy change record. When the saved decision names
172	// a policy version whose full content has no change record before the
173	// target, ErrVersionNotFound is returned; a newer version is never
174	// substituted, and a request the envelope would reject never masks the
175	// missing version.
176	//
177	// The fingerprint only proves the material matches its checkpoint; it
178	// cannot stand in for evaluating the request itself. So even when the
179	// declared version exists and carries an otherwise matching allow policy,
180	// the recomputation enforces the same request rules as the online
181	// decision: a disabled subject, an organization mismatch, a missing
182	// subject or resource organization or identifier, an empty action, and an
183	// illegal resource scope all deny, with the same reasons and precedence as
184	// Decide. Such a rejection uses no policies, so the recomputed decision
185	// reports version 0 with no matched policies; it is then compared field by
186	// field with the preserved original and may come back inconsistent.
187	func RecheckDecisionOffline(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint, seq int) (OfflineDecisionReview, error) {
188		if org == "" {
189			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, ErrMissingOrganization
190		}
191		// Validate the whole export first. A subject-filtered page, a fragment
192		// missing the beginning, or a checkpoint that does not pin the records
193		// all fail here, as does any corruption after the target.
194		m, err := verifyAuditMaterial(org, records, cp)
195		if err != nil {
196			return OfflineDecisionReview{}, err
197		}
198		return recheckVerifiedOffline(m, seq)
199	}
200	
201	// policiesBefore searches records[:limit] for the policy change record that
202	// published version and returns a detached copy of its full content. The
203	// gapless chain validation guarantees records are in sequence order.
204	func policiesBefore(records []AuditRecord, limit, version int) ([]Policy, bool) {
205		for i := 0; i < limit; i++ {
206			r := &records[i]
207			if r.Kind != AuditPolicyChange || r.Change == nil {
208				continue
209			}
210			if r.Change.Version == version {
211				return append([]Policy(nil), r.Change.Policies...), true
212			}
213		}
214		return nil, false
215	}
216	
217	// cloneDecisionValue returns a decision detached from the input's matched
218	// slice. The list is detached whenever it is non-nil, including a non-nil
219	// empty list that still has spare capacity, so an append by one receiver
220	// can never reach another copy.
221	func cloneDecisionValue(d Decision) Decision {
222		d.Matched = cloneStrings(d.Matched)
223		return d
224	}
225	
226	// decisionsEqual compares every decision field. A nil matched list and an
227	// empty matched list describe the same set of hits.
228	func decisionsEqual(a, b Decision) bool {
229		if a.Allowed != b.Allowed || a.Reason != b.Reason || a.Version != b.Version {
230			return false
231		}
232		if len(a.Matched) == 0 && len(b.Matched) == 0 {
233			return true
234		}
235		if len(a.Matched) != len(b.Matched) {
236			return false
237		}
238		for i := range a.Matched {
239			if a.Matched[i] != b.Matched[i] {
240				return false
241			}
242		}
243		return true
244	}
245	
246	// verifyAuditObserver, when non-nil, is invoked once for every complete
247	// VerifyAudit chain validation performed by this package. It exists so
248	// tests can pin the review flow to a single chain pass per invocation:
249	// decode and review must share one verification, never validate the same
250	// material twice. It is a test seam, not production behavior — it is nil in
251	// normal use and observes nothing about validation's result.
252	var verifyAuditObserver func()
253	
254	// SetVerifyAuditObserverForTesting installs observe as the chain-validation
255	// observer: it is invoked once for every complete VerifyAudit pass the
256	// package performs. The returned function restores the previous observer
257	// (the normal nil observer). It exists only so tests can pin the offline
258	// review flow to one chain validation per command invocation; it has no
259	// effect on validation itself or on any result.
260	func SetVerifyAuditObserverForTesting(observe func()) (restore func()) {
261		prev := verifyAuditObserver
262		verifyAuditObserver = observe
263		return func() { verifyAuditObserver = prev }
264	}

1	// This file pins down the decoder's handling of a corrupted decision
2	// *reason string length*: archives whose outer framing, declared payload
3	// length and checksum are all correct, but where one decision's Reason
4	// length word promises bytes the payload does not contain, or where that
5	// length word itself is only partly saved. The reason is an ordinary
6	// length-prefixed stringField in the wire format, so this protection is the
7	// generic string boundary read — but a decision reason is the field an
8	// auditor actually reads, and it had no regression of its own the way the
9	// internal list counts and the single-byte markers do.
10	//
11	// Two failure classes must stay distinct. A reason length that cannot be
12	// satisfied by the remaining material makes the archive unreadable: the
13	// read must fail with ErrInvalidArchive (matched by errors.Is), never
14	// panic, never provision the declared (up to 4294967295) byte count, and
15	// never treat the missing tail as an empty reason and continue. Flipping a
16	// byte inside reason *content* while leaving every length and marker legal
17	// instead keeps the structure readable and fails as content against the
18	// original fingerprints and retained checkpoint: ErrInvalidRange, never
19	// ErrInvalidArchive.
20	//
21	// As with the list- and marker-corruption files, every structural corruption
22	// below is reframed with a consistent outer length and checksum. That
23	// forces the observed failure to come from being unable to read the reason
24	// completely, not from the framing-level checksum check.
25	package darksafe
26	
27	import (
28		"bytes"
29		"encoding/binary"
30		"errors"
31		"reflect"
32		"runtime"
33		"strings"
34		"testing"
35	)
36	
37	// locateReasonLengthWord returns the payload offset of the 4-byte length
38	// word that prefixes reason's content bytes. The reason content must occur
39	// exactly once, so the length word immediately before it is unambiguous; a
40	// format or fixture change that breaks this fails loudly instead of
41	// corrupting the wrong field.
42	func locateReasonLengthWord(t *testing.T, payload []byte, reason string) int {
43		t.Helper()
44		needle := []byte(reason)
45		idx := bytes.Index(payload, needle)
46		if idx < 4 {
47			t.Fatalf("decision reason %q not found in payload", reason)
48		}
49		if bytes.Index(payload[idx+1:], needle) >= 0 {
50			t.Fatalf("decision reason %q must be unique for an unambiguous locate", reason)
51		}
52		return idx - 4
53	}
54	
55	// reasonChainFixture builds complete, valid material: one policy publish
56	// followed by one decision carrying the unique, non-empty laterReason. It
57	// returns the encoded archive, the caller's retained checkpoint and the
58	// reason text the tests corrupt.
59	func reasonChainFixture(t *testing.T, laterReason string) ([]byte, Checkpoint) {
60		t.Helper()
61		recs, cp := syntheticChain("acme", []func(int) (string, *PolicyChange, *DecisionRecord){
62			func(seq int) (string, *PolicyChange, *DecisionRecord) {
63				return AuditPolicyChange, &PolicyChange{
64					Version:  1,
65					Policies: []Policy{allowPolicy("p1", "u1", "read", "org/a", false)},
66				}, nil
67			},
68			func(seq int) (string, *PolicyChange, *DecisionRecord) {
69				return AuditDecision, nil, &DecisionRecord{
70					Request:  request("acme", "u1", "r1", "org/a", "read"),
71					Decision: Decision{Allowed: true, Reason: laterReason, Matched: []string{"p1"}, Version: 1},
72				}
73			},
74		})
75		archive, err := EncodeAuditArchive("acme", recs, cp)
76		if err != nil {
77			t.Fatalf("encode reason fixture: %v", err)
78		}
79		return archive, cp
80	}

82	// TestArchiveDecisionReasonLengthCorruption covers the shapes that make a
83	// decision reason unreadable while the outer length and checksum still
84	// hold: a declared reason length larger than the bytes left (by one and by
85	// a wide margin), the maximum uint32 length on a body that could never hold
86	// it, and a length word physically cut off partway. Each must fail as
87	// ErrInvalidArchive with nil records — not ErrInvalidRange, not a crash,
88	// not a phantom allocation, and not an empty-reason continuation — and must
89	// leave both the archive bytes and the retained checkpoint untouched.
90	func TestArchiveDecisionReasonLengthCorruption(t *testing.T) {
91		reason := "the-decision-reason-b7d2"
92		good, cp := reasonChainFixture(t, reason)
93		basePayload := payloadOf(t, good)
94		lenAt := locateReasonLengthWord(t, basePayload, reason)
95		if got := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(basePayload[lenAt:]); got != uint32(len(reason)) {

100		// outer length and checksum, and asserts the whole read fails as an
101		// unreadable archive without delivering records or rewriting inputs.
102		expectInvalid := func(name, wantSubstr string, mutate func(p []byte) []byte) {
103			t.Helper()
104			payload := mutate(append([]byte(nil), basePayload...))
105			data := framePayload(payload)
106			dataSnapshot := append([]byte(nil), data...)
107			cpSnapshot := cp
108	
109			got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(data, "acme", cp)
110			if !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidArchive) {
111				t.Fatalf("%s: err = %v, want ErrInvalidArchive", name, err)
112			}
113			if errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidRange) {
114				t.Fatalf("%s: an unreadable reason counted as a content error: %v", name, err)
115			}
116			if got != nil {
117				t.Fatalf("%s: returned %d records on a damaged reason, want nil", name, len(got))
118			}
119			if wantSubstr != "" && !strings.Contains(err.Error(), wantSubstr) {
120				t.Fatalf("%s: err = %q, want substring %q", name, err.Error(), wantSubstr)
121			}
122			if !bytes.Equal(data, dataSnapshot) {
123				t.Fatalf("%s: failed decode rewrote the archive bytes", name)
124			}
125			if cp != cpSnapshot {
126				t.Fatalf("%s: failed decode rewrote the retained checkpoint", name)
127			}
128		}
129	
130		// Bytes left after the reason length word, which a complete reason plus
131		// the matched list, version and two fingerprints would occupy.
132		remaining := len(basePayload) - (lenAt + 4)
133	
134		// The length word is intact but promises more reason bytes than remain.
135		// The payload itself keeps its length, so the only thing wrong is that
136		// the reason cannot be read in full: the error must originate at that
137		// string boundary, not at the (recomputed, valid) checksum.
138		expectInvalid("reason length exceeds remaining by one", "truncated archive payload",
139			func(p []byte) []byte {
140				binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(p[lenAt:], uint32(remaining+1))
141				return p
142			})
143		expectInvalid("reason length far exceeds remaining", "truncated archive payload",
144			func(p []byte) []byte {
145				binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(p[lenAt:], uint32(remaining)+1_000_000)
146				return p
147			})
148	
149		// 4294967295 reason bytes on this small body must be rejected on the
150		// remaining-byte bound, without enumerating or provisioning the phantom
151		// bytes. Measure the error path: a regression that trusted the length
152		// would try to allocate gigabytes here.
153		measureHuge := func(name string, mutate func(p []byte) []byte) {
154			t.Helper()
155			payload := mutate(append([]byte(nil), basePayload...))
156			data := framePayload(payload)
157			var before, after runtime.MemStats
158			runtime.GC()
159			runtime.ReadMemStats(&before)
160			got, err := DecodeAuditArchive(data, "acme", cp)
161			runtime.ReadMemStats(&after)
162			if !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidArchive) || got != nil {
163				t.Fatalf("%s: records=%v err=%v, want ErrInvalidArchive, nil", name, got, err)
164			}
165			if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "truncated archive payload") {
166				t.Fatalf("%s: err = %q, want the reason read-boundary rejection", name, err.Error())
167			}
168			if alloc := after.TotalAlloc - before.TotalAlloc; alloc > 16<<20 {
169				t.Fatalf("%s allocated %d bytes, want a small error path", name, alloc)
170			}
171		}
172		measureHuge("max uint32 reason length on small body",
173			func(p []byte) []byte {
174				binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(p[lenAt:], 0xffffffff)
175				return p
176			})
177	
178		// The length word is only partly saved: cut the payload 0..3 bytes into
179		// the word (and beyond, for the fully-missing end) and reframe. The
180		// reader cannot even learn the declared length, so each cut must be a
181		// truncation error rather than a zero/empty reason.
182		for _, cutIntoWord := range []int{0, 1, 2, 3} {
183			name := "reason length word cut with " + string(rune('0'+cutIntoWord)) + " of 4 bytes present"
184			expectInvalid(name, "truncated archive payload",
185				func(p []byte) []byte { return p[:lenAt+cutIntoWord] })
186		}
187	}

189	// TestArchiveTinyReasonHugeLengthNoAllocation is the dedicated emphasis of
190	// the allocation requirement: a hand-built, tiny archive that reaches a
191	// decision and then declares its reason to be 4294967295 bytes long with no

1	// This file pins down the decoder's handling of corrupted *internal list
2	// lengths*: archives whose outer framing, declared payload length and
3	// checksum are all correct, but where a count declared inside the payload
4	// cannot be satisfied by the bytes that follow. Three lists carry counts:
5	// the material's record list, a policy change's policy list, and the string
6	// lists used for subject roles and matched policies.
7	//
8	// Every corruption below is reframed with a consistent outer length and
9	// checksum, so exercising these cases proves the protection comes from
10	// decoding the payload's own structure rather than from the framing-level
11	// samples in audit_archive_test.go. A count the body cannot satisfy, a
12	// count word cut off mid-read, and a complete early item followed by an
13	// incomplete later item are all unreadable archives: DecodeAuditArchive
14	// must return ErrInvalidArchive (matched by errors.Is) and nil records,
15	// never a prefix and never a crash or hostile allocation.
16	package darksafe
17	
18	import (
19		"bytes"
20		"crypto/sha256"
21		"encoding/binary"
22		"errors"
23		"reflect"
24		"runtime"
25		"strings"
26		"testing"
27	)

29	// listSite locates one length-counted list inside a payload, in payload
30	// byte offsets. itemEnds marks the byte just past each complete item.
31	type listSite struct {
32		markerAt int
33		countAt  int // -1 when the list is encoded nil
34		itemEnds []int
35	}
36	
37	// payloadInspector walks the known-good, two-record fixture payload in
38	// encode order. It exists only to locate the bytes a test corrupts; it
39	// mirrors archiveWriter, so a format change moves these tests off their
40	// target rather than silently corrupting the wrong field.
41	type payloadInspector struct {
42		b   []byte
43		pos int
44	}
45	
46	func (c *payloadInspector) u32() int {
47		v := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(c.b[c.pos : c.pos+4]))
48		c.pos += 4
49		return v
50	}
51	
52	func (c *payloadInspector) str() {
53		n := c.u32()
54		c.pos += n
55	}
56	
57	func (c *payloadInspector) marker() byte {
58		m := c.b[c.pos]
59		c.pos++
60		return m
61	}
62	
63	func (c *payloadInspector) stringListSite() listSite {
64		s := listSite{markerAt: c.pos, countAt: -1}
65		if c.marker() == archiveTagNil {
66			return s
67		}
68		s.countAt = c.pos
69		n := c.u32()
70		s.itemEnds = make([]int, 0, n)
71		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
72			c.str()
73			s.itemEnds = append(s.itemEnds, c.pos)
74		}
75		return s
76	}
77	
78	func (c *payloadInspector) policySite() {
79		c.str() // ID
80		c.str() // Subject
81		c.str() // Action
82		c.str() // Scope
83		c.str() // Effect
84		c.pos++ // Recursive bool
85		c.str() // ResourceID
86	}
87	
88	func (c *payloadInspector) policyListSite() listSite {
89		s := listSite{markerAt: c.pos, countAt: -1}

91			return s
92		}
93		s.countAt = c.pos

97			c.policySite()

101	}

103	// inspectTwoRecordPayload locates the four counted lists in the fixture

172	// fixtureSites are the four counted lists in the two-record fixture.
173	type fixtureSites struct {
174		records  listSite
175		policies listSite
176		roles    listSite

180	// framePayload wraps a (possibly corrupted) payload with correct outer
181	// framing, declared length and checksum, so the failure under test is
182	// always internal list decoding rather than framing.
183	func framePayload(payload []byte) []byte {
184		out := append([]byte(nil), archiveMagic...)
185		var lb [4]byte
186		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(lb[:], uint32(len(payload)))
187		out = append(out, lb[:]...)
188		out = append(out, payload...)
189		sum := sha256.Sum256(payload)
190		return append(out, sum[:]...)
191	}

194	func payloadOf(t *testing.T, archive []byte) []byte {
195		t.Helper()
196		magicLen := len(archiveMagic)

244	// ErrInvalidArchive with nil records — even when a complete, readable
245	// prefix (a full policy change and decision) precedes the damage.

255		expectInvalid := func(name, wantSubstr string, mutate func(p []byte) []byte) {

48	// "organization has no published version" denial.
49	//

53	// even for a disabled subject. Once the version is in hand, the same
54	// envelope checks run before policy evaluation, so a rejection reports
55	// version 0 with no matched policies regardless of what the version
56	// contains. Evaluation itself is the historical policy set only: deny
57	// overrides allow, matched identifiers are sorted, resource restrictions
58	// narrow rather than replace scope matching, and subject roles never stand
59	// in for an organization policy.
60	func replayRecordedDecision(org string, req OrgRequest, version int, resolve resolveVersionPolicies) (Decision, replayStatus) {
61		if version == 0 {
62			// The original evaluation used no published version: replay the
63			// envelope rejections exactly, in their recorded order, then the
64			// not-yet-published denial.
65			if d, ok := checkRequest(org, req); !ok {

- `TestArchiveReadRejectsCategoryContentMismatch` — 用 `archiveWriter` 手工构造长度/校验和正确、组织/序号/前后指纹/检查点全部一致、字段完整可读的归档，覆盖全部非法组合：所需内容缺失、只带另一类内容、两类同时存在、出现两种公开类别之外的记录。两个读取入口都必须返回 `ErrInvalidRange`（不得是 `ErrInvalidArchive`），且不交付任何记录或 `VerifiedAuditMaterial`。
- `TestArchiveMismatchAfterValidDecisionDiscardsPrefix` — 非法记录位于一条正常决策之后时整份读取仍失败、不先交付前缀；同一条正常前缀在配套检查点下单独归档则两个入口均正常返回并可复核。
- `TestArchiveLegalBoundaryCategoriesRead` — 合法对照：变更内容存在但策略集合为 nil（以及拒绝、version 0、无命中列表的决策，含 nil 与空列表两种形态）仍正常读取；空列表/零值不被当成内容缺失。
- `TestVerifiedArchiveReadLeavesInconsistencyToReview` — 材料与检查点一致即读取成功，合法决策日后复核得到不一致结论只在复核阶段报告，不被读取拒绝；两个入口成功含义一致。
